introduction: A feud between Verona's Capulet and Montague families governs the streets, friendships and marriage prospects of the younger generation. Romeo, a Montague, enters a Capulet celebration and discovers a love that makes the inherited quarrel suddenly intolerable. Juliet must negotiate her parents' expectations while deciding what promises she can make for herself. Friends, a nurse and a friar try to shape the lovers' course, but private decisions repeatedly collide with public violence, hurried arrangements and messages whose timing matters desperately.

fullSynopsis.text: The Chorus announces that the deaths of two lovers will end their families' ancient feud. In Verona, a quarrel between Capulet and Montague servants escalates into another public brawl, and Prince Escalus threatens death for further disturbances. Romeo Montague, absent from the fight, is absorbed in unreturned love for Rosaline. Benvolio encourages him to compare her with other women at Capulet's feast. Meanwhile Paris asks to marry Capulet's daughter Juliet, not yet fourteen. Capulet initially advises waiting and seeking her consent; Lady Capulet and the Nurse urge Juliet to consider the match.

Romeo attends the feast with Benvolio and Mercutio, despite a foreboding that the evening will begin a fatal course. Tybalt recognizes him and wants violence, but Capulet restrains him. Romeo and Juliet meet, exchange kisses and only afterwards learn that they belong to enemy households. Romeo returns secretly to the Capulet garden and overhears Juliet questioning the barrier of their names. They declare mutual love and arrange to marry. Friar Lawrence questions Romeo's sudden abandonment of Rosaline but agrees to help, hoping the alliance will reconcile the families. The Nurse carries messages and arranges Romeo's access to Juliet after their secret wedding.

Tybalt challenges Romeo, who refuses to fight his new kinsman without revealing the marriage. Mercutio takes the refusal as dishonourable and fights Tybalt himself. Romeo intervenes, but Tybalt wounds Mercutio under his arm. Mercutio dies cursing both houses. In revenge, Romeo kills Tybalt and flees; the Prince banishes him from Verona. Juliet's first horror at her cousin's death gives way to loyalty to her husband and anguish at his exile. Lawrence prevents Romeo from killing himself and devises a hopeful future: one night with Juliet, then refuge in Mantua until the marriage can be revealed and a pardon sought.

Capulet, treating Juliet's sorrow as grief for Tybalt, abruptly promises her to Paris. After Romeo and Juliet's dawn farewell, her mother announces the wedding. Juliet refuses, provoking her father's threats of disowning her. Her mother withdraws support, and the Nurse advises marrying Paris because Romeo is effectively lost to her. Juliet ceases to confide in the Nurse and turns to Lawrence. He gives her a potion that will make her appear dead for forty-two hours: her family will place her in their tomb, and Romeo, informed by letter, will collect her when she wakes. Juliet accepts this desperate alternative to a second marriage.

Juliet pretends obedience, and Capulet advances the wedding from Thursday to the next morning. Alone, she imagines poison, suffocation and madness in the family vault, but drinks the potion. The Nurse finds her apparently dead, and wedding preparations become funeral arrangements. Balthasar sees her burial and brings the news to Romeo in Mantua. Determined to die beside her, Romeo buys poison from an impoverished apothecary and returns to Verona. Lawrence then discovers that Friar John never delivered his explanatory letter: officials confined him because they suspected plague infection. Lawrence goes alone to the tomb to retrieve Juliet as she wakes.

At the tomb, Paris mistakes Romeo's arrival for an attempt to dishonour the dead and tries to arrest him. Romeo kills Paris, lays him beside Juliet, then drinks poison and dies before she awakens. Lawrence arrives too late and urges the waking Juliet to leave, but flees when he hears the watch. Juliet stays and kills herself with Romeo's dagger. The families and Prince assemble; Lawrence's account, the servants' testimony and Romeo's letter establish what happened. Montague also reports his wife's death from grief at Romeo's exile. Capulet and Montague clasp hands and promise golden memorials to the lovers. Their reconciliation brings a sorrowful peace, while decisions about pardon and punishment remain to be made.

acts.label: ACT I
acts.summary: The feud erupts through the servants into a street fight involving Tybalt and Benvolio. The Prince demands peace on pain of death. Romeo tells Benvolio of the woman who refuses his love, and an encounter with Capulet's invitation-bearing servant leads them towards the feast where Rosaline will be present. Paris asks to marry Juliet, but Capulet advises patience and courtship; Juliet agrees only to look at him as her mother requests. Mercutio mocks Romeo's dreams in the Queen Mab speech, while Romeo fears a fatal consequence of the evening. At the feast Capulet restrains Tybalt, and Romeo and Juliet fall in love before discovering one another's family names.

acts.label: ACT II
acts.summary: The Chorus contrasts Romeo's abandoned desire with the mutual love that must now overcome hostile circumstances. Romeo slips away from his friends and enters Capulet's garden. Juliet, unaware of his presence, questions the force of their family names; when he reveals himself, they exchange vows and arrange a marriage. Friar Lawrence rebukes Romeo's sudden change from Rosaline but consents to marry them in the hope of ending the feud. Mercutio and Benvolio discuss Tybalt's challenge before Romeo joins their wordplay. The Nurse meets Romeo, receives the wedding arrangements and promises to obtain a rope ladder. After teasingly delaying her report to Juliet, she sends her to Lawrence, who leads the lovers away to marry.

acts.label: ACT III
acts.summary: Romeo refuses Tybalt's challenge because their secret marriage has made them kin. Mercutio fights instead and is mortally wounded when Romeo tries to separate them. Romeo then kills Tybalt, and the Prince sentences him to exile. Juliet learns the news from the Nurse and struggles between grief for her cousin and loyalty to her husband. Lawrence checks Romeo's suicidal despair and proposes that he visit Juliet before escaping to Mantua, where he can await reconciliation and pardon. Capulet meanwhile fixes a marriage with Paris for Thursday. After the lovers part at dawn, Juliet refuses the proposed wedding, faces her father's threats, and loses confidence in the Nurse when she recommends Paris.

acts.label: ACT IV
acts.summary: Juliet encounters Paris at Lawrence's cell, then threatens to kill herself if no remedy can prevent a second marriage. Lawrence provides a potion to imitate death for forty-two hours and plans to notify Romeo so they can recover her from the family tomb. At home Juliet feigns submission, delighting Capulet, who moves the wedding to the following morning. She dismisses her attendants and confronts fears that the potion is poison or that she may wake alone among the dead. She drinks it nevertheless. Capulet's household prepares through the night, only for the Nurse to find Juliet apparently lifeless. The family and Paris mourn as Lawrence directs the conversion of the wedding into a funeral.

acts.label: ACT V
acts.summary: Balthasar tells Romeo that Juliet has been buried. Receiving no letter from Lawrence, Romeo buys forbidden poison from a poor apothecary and returns to Verona. Lawrence discovers that Friar John was prevented from carrying his message by a suspected plague quarantine and hurries to the tomb. Paris challenges Romeo there and is killed. Romeo drinks the poison beside the still-sleeping Juliet. Lawrence arrives as she wakes, but leaves when she refuses to flee the approaching watch. She kills herself with Romeo's dagger. The Prince hears the surviving witnesses and reads Romeo's corroborating letter. Montague reports his wife's death; the fathers reconcile over their children, while further judgement is deferred.

framing.label: THE PROLOGUE
framing.summary: The Chorus places the action in Verona and identifies two equally prominent households whose ancient quarrel has broken into fresh violence. It announces in advance that their children will become lovers, die, and thereby end the parents' feud. The audience is asked to attend patiently as the performance traces both the lovers' course and the continuing family rage.
